evidence: admin.py:88-94 _record_to_wire emits key "groups" (list, or None for corrupt tagged records, [] for untagged) alongside memory_id, memory_type, timestamp. memory_admin.html:739 reads m.groups (renderGroups), and lines 640-641 handle non-array as unreadable and empty as untagged, matching the emitted shape. last_hit_date is emitted in the tool-memory branch (not re-read here); the claim concerns the groups field name and shape, which match.

admin.py:93 _record_to_wire always sets "groups" to record_groups(metadata) (a list of strings, _memory_groups.py:60-74) or, if empty, None for a tagged record (is_tagged, line 48-50) and [] for untagged. So the wire values are a list of strings, [] or null. memory_admin.html:628-636 and 640-643 treat any non-array (null, missing key, other type) as unreadable and [] as untagged, which matches the claim. I did not separately read get_memory, but I did not find any other place in admin.py that builds "groups" (the grep for groups shows only line 93 in the wire construction).

server.py:729 get_memory tool calls memory_admin.get_memory, which returns _record_to_wire (admin.py:199-206), the same serializer list_memories uses (admin.py:188-195). It sets groups = record_groups(metadata) or (None if is_tagged(metadata) else []) (admin.py:93): a list of names for tagged records, [] for untagged, null for corrupt tagged records. Both tools therefore show the same three states.

Retrieval is search_similar_usage (agent_memory.py:267-280) and search_text_memories (:464-472). Both AND in self._scope_filter(), which is non-None whenever group_scope is set (:138-143). factory.py:173 sets group_scope whenever rule_sets is not None, and the scope is () with no selection (factory.py:91-95). _memory_groups.scope_filter (:77-86) accepts only untagged records ({memory_tagged: {$ne: True}}) or ones where memory_groups $contains a group name. A record with memory_tagged True is not untagged. 'Unreadable' means is_tagged is True but record_groups (:60-74) returns []. That happens when the key is missing, the value is not a list or string, or the list holds no strings. In each case memory_groups cannot $contains a string group name, so no rule set retrieves it. Mixed lists and plain-string values are read by record_groups, so they are not 'unreadable'. Counterexample checked: the unfiltered get_recent_memories and get_recent_text_memories (agent_memory.py:366, :514) are reached only through the /memories workflow command, which default.py:~120-138 restricts to administrators. It is a listing, not rule-set retrieval, so it does not break the claim. Not verified: how the installed ChromaDB version evaluates $contains on malformed metadata, which I did not run.

Retrieval scope is built by scope_filter (src/sqllens/_memory_groups.py:77-86). Every branch includes the untagged condition {memory_tagged: {$ne: True}}. With no groups it is that condition alone; with groups it is $or[untagged, ...contains]. Untagged records carry neither key (group_metadata, :36-45), so $ne True matches them. rule_sets.memory_groups_for (rule_sets.py:755-760) returns () for a rule set with no memory_groups or an absent one, so such a set still reads untagged records. agent_memory.py:138-143 applies the scope, or no filter at all when group_scope is None. Both retrieval queries, search_similar_usage (:267-276) and search_text_memories (:464-469), apply it. The other collection.get calls (:366, 514, 571) are admin listing or lookup by id, not rule-set retrieval. I found no rule set configuration that excludes an untagged memory. A record marked tagged but with an unreadable group list is not untagged, and the UI text treats it separately.

importer.py _plan (lines 142-159): a matched item creates no new record. For every matching target it unions the item's groups into target.groups. If any target changed, plan.updated += 1; otherwise plan.skipped_duplicate += 1. Changed stored records are written via store.add_groups (212-213). Duplicates within the same import merge into the earlier item's _Target. admin.py:326-327 maps updated to updated_count and skipped_duplicate to duplicate_count. This matches the UI text: the duplicate is not saved again, its groups are added to every entry it matches, it counts as updated, and a duplicate that changes no groups is skipped.

src/sqllens/memory/admin.py:370-381: in the CSV branch, lossy=True when docs is non-empty (line 371-372), and when csv_groups_dropped_warning returns non-None (377-379). exporter.py:38-45 counts tagged pairs and tagged docs; non-None when any has groups. So CSV with schema docs or tagged pairs is marked lossy:true, matching the HTML text at memory_admin.html:320-322. Untagged pairs only are not lossy, consistent with the claim.
